arxiv-2312-00820.title: Non-Cross Diffusion for Semantic Consistency
arxiv-2312-00820.creator: Ziyang Zheng, Ruiyuan GaoQiang XuThe Chinese University of Hong Kong {zyzheng23,rygao,qxu}@cse.cuhk.edu.hk
arxiv-2312-00820.description: Abstract In diffusion models, deviations from a straight generative flow are a common issue, resulting in semantic inconsistencies and suboptimal generations. arxiv-2312-15273.title: Benefit from public unlabeled data: A Frangi filtering-based pretraining network for 3D cerebrovascular segmentation Journal: Medical Image Analysis
arxiv-2312-15273.creator: Gen Shi, Hao Lu, Hui Hui, Jie Tian
arxiv-2312-15273.description: Abstract The precise cerebrovascular segmentation in time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography (TOF-MRA) data is crucial for clinically computer-aided diagnosis. However, the sparse distribution of cerebrovascular structures in TOF-MRA results in an exceedingly high cost for manual data labeling. The use of unlabeled TOF-MRA data holds the potential to enhance model performance significantly.

arxiv-2406-04253.description: Abstract 3D modeling has long been an important area in computer vision and computer graphics. arxiv-2406-20071.title: SAT and Lattice Reduction for Integer Factorization
arxiv-2406-20071.creator: Yameen Ajani, Curtis Bright
arxiv-2406-20071.description: Abstract . The difficulty of factoring large integers into primes is the basis for cryptosystems such as RSA. Due to the widespread popularity of RSA, there have been many proposed attacks on the factorization problem such as side-channel attacks where some bits of the prime factors are available.

arxiv-2409-01590.title: Kerr-magnon-assisted asymptotic stationary photon-phonon squeezing
arxiv-2409-01590.creator: Shi-fan Qi, Jun Jing
arxiv-2409-01590.description: Abstract Bosonic two-mode squeezed states are paradigmatic entangled states in continuous variable systems, which have broad applications in quantum information processing. In this work, we propose a photon-phonon squeezing protocol assisted by a Kerr magnon within a hybrid cavity magnomechanical system.

arxiv-2502-04667.title: Compositional Generalization from Learned Skills via CoT Training: A Theoretical and Structural Analysis for Reasoning
arxiv-2502-04667.creator: Xinhao Yao, Ruifeng Ren, Yun Liao, Lizhong Ding, Yong Liu
arxiv-2502-04667.description: Abstract Chain-of-Thought (CoT) training has markedly advanced the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs), yet the mechanisms by which CoT training enhances generalization remain inadequately understood. In this work, we demonstrate that compositional generalization is fundamental: models systematically combine simpler learned skills during CoT training to address novel and more complex problems.

In general, at a long distance r r from the source, the near-surface field is mostly contributed by the geometrical optics term (describing the radiation pattern), a guided wave, and the higher-order reactive contribution referred to as the Norton wave.

pmc-13437306.title: Complications of pulsed-field ablation for atrial fibrillation: a narrative structured review
pmc-13437306.creator: Jiangyao Li, Jia Gao, Rui Wang
pmc-13437306.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) has been adopted at remarkable speed as a non-thermal approach for pulmonary vein isolation in atrial fibrillation (AF). Its mechanism—irreversible electroporation—preferentially injures cardiomyocytes while theoretically sparing adjacent heat-sensitive structures. Landmark randomised trial data (ADVENT) and large prospective registries (MANIFEST-17K; MANIFEST-PF) confirm that PFA is non-inferior to conventional thermal ablation for arrhythmia freedom and carries an overall favourable safety profile, with particularly low rates of atrooesophageal fistula and pulmonary vein stenosis.
